biological.citation: STXBP1-Related Disorders: Clinical Presentation, Molecular Function, Treatment, and Future Directions (PMID: 38137001)
biological.summary: STXBP1 encodes Munc18-1 protein, which is essential for synaptic vesicle fusion and neurotransmitter release. Pathogenic variants result in haploinsufficiency and impaired neurotransmitter release, leading to dysfunction in neuronal communication.

biological.citation: Reduced MUNC18-1 Levels, Synaptic Proteome Changes, and Altered Network Activity in STXBP1-Related Disorder Patient Neurons (PMID: 38298782)
biological.summary: iPSC-derived neurons from 6 STXBP1-RD patients showed reduced MUNC18-1 RNA and protein levels, dysregulation of synaptic proteins, and altered network activity patterns. Proteome-wide screening identified dysregulation of proteins related to synapse function and RNA processes, with patient clustering suggesting distinctive pathobiology.

biological.citation: STXBP1 encephalopathy: Connecting neurodevelopmental disorders with α-synucleinopathies? (PMID: 31221716)
biological.summary: STXBP1 (Munc18-1) controls the self-replicating aggregation of α-synuclein, a presynaptic protein involved in neurodegenerative diseases. STXBP1 functions as a molecular chaperone for α-synuclein, linking early-onset neurodevelopmental disorders with synucleinopathies.

biological.citation: ASHG 2023 - α-Synuclein pathology in Drosophila melanogaster is exacerbated by haploinsufficiency of Rop: Connecting STXBP1 encephalopathy with α-synucleinopathies (T. Matsuoka et al.)
biological.summary: In Drosophila, haploinsufficiency of Rop (STXBP1 homolog) exacerbates α-synuclein aggregation and pathology. Rop heterozygous flies showed increased insoluble α-synuclein, reduced dopamine neurons, and impaired motor function. Trehalose feeding reversed these phenotypes, demonstrating a molecular interaction between STXBP1 and α-synuclein in vivo.

biological.citation: ASHG 2019 - Humanized STXBP1 animal models as a precision medicine approach to detecting pathogenicity in clinical variants (C. Hopkins et al.)
biological.summary: Humanized C. elegans model with human STXBP1 inserted as replacement for unc-18 showed 100% rescue of function by electrophysiology (4-fold increase from knockout) and 100% rescue in thrashing assays. Pathogenic variants (p.R292H, p.R406H, p.R388X) showed quantifiable functional defects in heterozygotes, with p.R388X displaying dominant-negative activity.

biological.citation: ASHG 2019 - Zebrafish modeling for the clinic: Rapid in vivo functional testing of patient variants for clinical applications (B. Jussila et al.)
biological.summary: Zebrafish CRISPR/Cas9 knockout of stxbp1a (STXBP1 ortholog) was used to model pediatric epilepsy and encephalopathy. Morpholino knockdown coupled with transient mRNA rescue of variant cDNA enabled rapid functional assessment of pathogenic and VUS alleles in an intact animal model with ~95% conservation to human disease genes.

biological.citation: Delineating clinical and developmental outcomes in STXBP1-related disorders (PMID: 38015929)
biological.summary: Natural history study of 162 individuals with STXBP1-related disorders (1281 cumulative patient-years) revealed genotype-phenotype correlations: protein-truncating variants and deletions showed infantile spasms with seizure remission, while missense variants showed focal seizures and ongoing seizures. Age-dependent anti-seizure medication response was documented, with phenobarbital, levetiracetam, topiramate, and ACTH effective in first year of life.

biological.citation: HSV-1 latency-associated transcript miR-H3 and miR-H4 target STXBP1 and GABBR2 genes (PMID: 37668872)
biological.summary: HSV-1 LAT-encoded microRNAs miR-H3 and miR-H4 directly target STXBP1 3'UTR. Overexpression of miR-H3, miR-H4, or LAT significantly decreased STXBP1 gene expression (0.0593-0.84 fold reduction). Luciferase assays confirmed miR-H3 reduces Renilla expression through STXBP1 3'UTR binding (0.62-fold reduction).

biological.citation: Identification of copper metabolism-related markers in Parkinson's disease (PMID: 39552415)
biological.summary: STXBP1 was identified as one of 9 hub genes related to copper metabolism in Parkinson's disease through integration of differentially expressed genes, copper-metabolism-related genes, and immune cell-related genes. ROC analysis showed high predictive accuracy for PD, and STXBP1 was highlighted as a potential therapeutic target in PD pathology.

biological.citation: ASHG 2023 - Comprehensive genomic analysis of a trios family study with an index child diagnosed with autism spectrum disorders (D. Manjegowda et al.)
biological.summary: Whole-exome sequencing of 27 Indian trios with autism spectrum disorder identified STXBP1 as one of multiple genes with SNVs contributing to ASD. Pathway analysis revealed dysregulation of glutamatergic synaptic transmission, linking STXBP1 variants to synaptic dysfunction in ASD pathophysiology.
